# Code of conduct

## The short version

Be decent. Assume the other person is trying to help. Argue about the code, not the person behind it.

This is a small project run by three people in their spare time. Nobody here is on call, nobody owes
you a fix, and a maintainer who says "not now" or "won't do" is answering, not being rude.

## Not acceptable

- Harassment, insults, or personal attacks — including about someone's experience level, English, or
  the state of their pull request.
- Discriminatory language or unwelcome attention of any kind.
- Publishing someone's private information.
- Demanding, entitled, or repeated pressure on maintainers. Bumping an issue every day is not
  urgency, it is noise.
- Posting someone else's device data, account details, or captures.

## Scope

This applies in issues, pull requests, commits, discussions, and the project's Discord — anywhere you
are acting as part of this project.

## Enforcement

Maintainers will remove, edit, or reject comments, commits, issues and pull requests that don't fit,
and will explain why when it isn't obvious. Repeated or severe behaviour gets a block.

To report something, contact a maintainer privately rather than escalating in the thread. Reports are
handled discreetly; the person who reports is never the one who has to justify themselves.

## Attribution

Adapted in spirit from the [Contributor Covenant](https://www.contributor-covenant.org), rewritten to
say what we actually mean.
